title: Processes and Jobs
subtitle: ps, top, kill, jobs, fg, bg — controlling what runs on your system
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
# ps: snapshot of current processes
ps              # your processes in current terminal
ps aux          # ALL processes from ALL users
ps aux | grep nginx   # find nginx processes
ps aux | grep -v grep | grep node   # find Node.js (exclude grep itself)

# ps output columns:
# USER  PID  %CPU  %MEM  VSZ   RSS  TTY  STAT  START  TIME  COMMAND
# root  1234  0.0   0.1  1024  512  ?    Ss    10:00  0:00  nginx
# PID = process ID (unique number for each process)

# top: live process viewer (q to quit)
top
top -u alice      # only alice's processes
top -p 1234       # watch specific PID

# htop: better version of top (may need to install)
htop

# pgrep: find PID by name
pgrep nginx       # print PIDs of nginx processes
pgrep -la node    # PIDs + command names

# kill sends a signal to a process by PID
kill 1234         # SIGTERM (15): graceful shutdown (please stop)
kill -9 1234      # SIGKILL (9): force kill (cannot be ignored)
kill -HUP 1234    # SIGHUP (1): reload config (for servers like nginx)

# pkill: kill by name
pkill nginx       # kill nginx gracefully
pkill -9 node     # force kill all node processes

# killall: same as pkill
killall -9 node

# Keyboard shortcuts
# Ctrl+C = send SIGINT to foreground process (graceful interrupt)
# Ctrl+Z = suspend foreground process (not kill — pauses it)

# Run a command in the background with &
python3 server.py &      # starts in background, prints PID
npm run dev &

# jobs: list background jobs in current shell
jobs
# [1]  Running    python3 server.py &
# [2]+ Stopped    vim notes.txt

# fg: bring a job to foreground
fg        # bring most recent job to foreground
fg %1     # bring job #1 to foreground

# bg: resume a stopped job in background
bg %1     # resume job #1 in background

# Typical workflow:
npm run dev &         # start dev server in background
git add . && git commit -m "feat: ..."  # do other work
fg                    # bring dev server back if needed

# nohup: keep running after terminal closes
nohup python3 server.py > server.log 2>&1 &

questions.question: A process is frozen and not responding to kill 1234 (SIGTERM). What do you do next?
questions.explanation: kill -9 sends SIGKILL, which cannot be caught or ignored by the process — the kernel terminates it immediately. Regular kill sends SIGTERM (15), which the process can ignore or delay acting on. Use -9 as a last resort after SIGTERM fails, since SIGKILL doesn't let the process clean up (close files, flush buffers, etc.).

faq.q: How do I find what is using port 3000?
faq.a: lsof -i :3000 — lists all processes with an open socket on port 3000. Or ss -tlnp | grep :3000 (faster). Then kill the PID shown. On macOS: lsof -ti :3000 | xargs kill -9 (one-liner to kill the process using port 3000).

examples: kill -HUP $(pgrep nginx) — reload nginx config without downtime, used in deployments
ps aux | grep Z — find 'zombie' processes (finished but not cleaned up, shown with Z in STAT)
